upperLimit.source: ICMR-NIN 2020 TUL as reported by CRN (2025), following US IOM/NASEM 1998 (100 mg/day). Stricter limits: EFSA 2023 UL 12 mg/day; UK advice max 10 mg/day from supplements; NHMRC draft 14 mg/day. App cautions from 10 mg/day of supplements

absorptionBoosters: whole pulses and sprouts instead of only split dals
whole grains, parboiled or brown rice instead of maida and white rice
dry-heat or short cooking (tandoor, grill, roast, quick saute, pressure cooking)
eating the cooking liquid (dal water, gravy, sambar, rasam)
a daily banana or other B6-rich fruit
animal-source foods for non-vegetarians (B6 absorbed slightly better than plant glucoside form)
absorptionBlockers: long-term isoniazid, cycloserine, penicillamine, anti-seizure medicines, theophylline or levodopa
warnings: Long-term high-dose vitamin B6 supplements can cause nerve damage (tingling, numbness or burning in hands and feet, unsteady walking).
UK advice is no more than 10 mg per day of vitamin B6 from supplements; EFSA's 2023 upper limit is 12 mg per day from all sources; ICMR and the US set 100 mg per day.
Vitamin B6 is found in many B-complex, nerve, magnesium, PMS, sports and energy products; add up all products you take.
If you take isoniazid or cycloserine (TB), levodopa (Parkinson's), anti-seizure medicines or theophylline, ask your doctor before taking vitamin B6.
Tingling or numbness in the hands or feet while taking a B6-containing product needs a doctor's review.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should only take vitamin B6 beyond a prenatal vitamin on a doctor's advice.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
